what_it_does: Analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) that use successive-approximation (SAR) architecture are efficient at converting analog signals to digital numbers, but achieving high precision (13 bits and above) requires a large capacitive array that draws heavy current from the input buffer. This forces the buffer to work harder, consuming most of the chip's power. This paper introduces continuous-time correlated level shifting in the input buffer: a compensation technique that adjusts the signal level continuously while maintaining linearity, allowing the buffer to drive the large capacitive load without needing extra power supply voltage. The result is a high-resolution SAR ADC with superior energy efficiency and dynamic range (105.4 dB SFDR—a measure of signal purity).
